I’ve had a lot of thoughts like, “What’s the point?” and sometimes I catch myself wondering if people would even notice if I disappeared.

On top of that, since I’ve been feeling this low, I’ve gotten stuck on this idea that my ex is cheating on me with another player. We’re not even officially together anymore, but I’m convinced she’s lying and secretly with him during scrims or tournaments. I check her socials, her match history, overanalyze every message. Deep down I know I don’t have proof, but the thought feels so real. That whole thing only started after I crashed mood‑wise; before this depressive stretch, I never thought like that.

It started about four months ago. At first it was just feeling low and worn out, like everything at the plant and at home was too much. I’d come home from the late shift and just sit in the car because I couldn’t make myself go inside. I stopped checking in with the guys on the line like I used to; I just don’t care about anything, even stuff I used to take pride in. My wife says I barely talk to her or the kids. I sleep badly, wake up at 3 or 4 in the morning with this heavy feeling in my chest, and I’ve lost about 15 pounds because I don’t feel like eating.

What really scares me is what’s been going through my head during this time. I’m convinced something awful is about to happen, like the world is winding down. It feels certain, like we’re all going to be wiped out soon and there’s no point in planning anything. Those thoughts only started once this dark mood hit and they’re there whenever the depression is at its worst. When I have a rare day that feels a bit lighter, that “end of the world” feeling backs off too.

D004-D015_h025.question:
It’s been a little over two months now that I just feel…flattened. I wake up exhausted, even after a full night, and most days I just lie there staring at the ceiling, thinking there’s no point in getting up. Driving the taxi used to be okay, I liked chatting with passengers, but lately I barely work. I’ve lost a lot of weight because I don’t feel like eating, and I don’t really care what happens to me. I keep thinking my life fell apart after the divorce and now it’s just downhill.

Since I’ve been this low, something else started happening. I’m convinced this woman who takes my cab sometimes is secretly in love with me. I know it sounds odd, but I’m sure the way she looks at me, the way she adjusts her hair, the times she “coincidentally” calls my car—those are signs. But these thoughts only started once I got really depressed and they kind of come and go with how bad my mood is. Before I sank like this, I never had beliefs like that about anyone. When my mood briefly lifts a bit, those ideas don’t feel as strong or real.
